judge_audit.independence_limit: Kappa here compares one semantic judge with the deterministic executable checker. It is not agreement between two independent LLM judge families; that remains a separate open experiment.
judge_audit.interpretation: The judge is reliable at noticing that something went wrong and materially less reliable at saying what owns it. That is precisely why ownership routing is advisory and the executable checker controls the release gate. Publishing the number is the point: a grader whose accuracy is unstated should not be trusted.
judge_audit.method: Recomputed from preserved episode artifacts. No new model calls were made, so this audit costs nothing and cannot drift from the results it describes.

verifier.honesty_note: These numbers come from 60 episodes containing 6 relevant failures. The rule was revised twice after inspecting its errors, so the final figures are in-sample and should be treated as a design signal rather than a generalisation. The revision history is published so the tuning is visible.
verifier.scope_limit: This catches say/do gaps — an asserted effect that never executed. It cannot catch omissions, where the agent simply never claims anything and never acts. The remaining miss is exactly that case: the agent told the caller to pay by evening and recorded nothing, so there was no false statement to detect. Omissions are the episode-level checker's job, which is why both layers exist.

metric_contract.inputs: The outcome the agent declared, and the scenario's accepted-disposition set.
metric_contract.name: Terminal outcome
metric_contract.output: Pass or fail. No partial credit.
metric_contract.question: Did the call end in one of the outcomes this scenario allows?
metric_contract.threshold: The declared outcome must be a member of the accepted set.
metric_contract.why: A conditional turned into a commitment, or a call that never terminates cleanly, is a business error even when the conversation sounds correct.

metric_contract.inputs: Every field the scenario names in expected_state, read from the isolated per-trial database after the run.
metric_contract.name: Backend state
metric_contract.output: Pass only if every named field matches exactly.
metric_contract.question: Does the account actually look the way it should after the call?
metric_contract.threshold: Exact match on all expected fields.
metric_contract.why: This is what makes a spoken claim falsifiable. The ledger either moved or it did not.

metric_contract.inputs: The scenario's required_actions, matched against the recorded tool events by name and arguments.
metric_contract.name: Required tool calls
metric_contract.output: Pass only if every required action has a matching executed call.
metric_contract.question: Did the agent call the tools this outcome requires, with the right arguments?
metric_contract.threshold: All required actions matched. Argument comparison normalises formats such as time windows.
metric_contract.why: Saying a promise was recorded is not recording it. This is the check the deployed agent failed six times.

metric_contract.inputs: Agent turns matched against the scenario's forbidden phrases, with credential terms cue-scoped so a correct refusal is not penalised.
metric_contract.name: Guardrails
metric_contract.output: Pass if no forbidden behaviour fired.
metric_contract.question: Did the agent do anything the scenario forbids?
metric_contract.threshold: Zero hits. A single hit fails the episode regardless of every other score.
metric_contract.why: Soliciting an OTP once is worse than failing the task. It cannot be averaged away.

metric_contract.inputs: The scenario's communication assertions, matched case-insensitively against agent speech.
metric_contract.name: Required disclosures
metric_contract.question: Did the agent say what policy requires it to say?
metric_contract.why: Regulated collections have mandatory disclosures. Currently unused by the EMI pack, and reported as such rather than quietly dropped.

metric_contract.inputs: Agent turn count, words per turn, exact repetitions, response latency.
metric_contract.name: Conversation quality
metric_contract.output: A 0–1 score: 0.15 penalty per overlong turn, 0.2 per exact repetition.
metric_contract.question: Was the call efficient for someone who did not want to be on it?
metric_contract.threshold: Reported separately. It cannot rescue a failed task, and a drop beyond the declared floor blocks release.
metric_contract.why: An agent can complete the task and still be unbearable. Keeping these axes apart is what stops one hiding the other.

metric_contract.inputs: Whether the simulated caller followed its hidden script and terminated through an allowed path.
metric_contract.name: Simulator validity
metric_contract.output: Valid or invalid. Invalid trials are excluded from scoring, not counted as agent failures.
metric_contract.question: Was this trial fair to score at all?
metric_contract.threshold: Checked before any other metric runs.
metric_contract.why: If the caller went off-policy, the agent's score is meaningless. Validation runs first by rule.

metric_contract.inputs: Full transcript, account facts, tool results, scenario policy.
metric_contract.name: Faithfulness, concision, progression
metric_contract.output: 1–4 scores with written rationale and a nominated failure component.
metric_contract.question: Of the things code cannot check, how good was this?
metric_contract.threshold: Diagnostic only. Never gates a release.
metric_contract.why: Judges are useful and fallible. Where the judge and the deterministic checker disagree, both readings are kept.
